issues.description: The solution repository implements the animal classes with names prefixed by 'Space' (SpaceSeal, SpacePig, SpaceGoat) while the problem statement and the template expect classes named Seal, Pig, and Goat. Additionally, the solution contains empty files named Seal.java, Pig.java, and Goat.java. This mismatch between expected class names and the solution's actual class names can confuse students (the template/Main references Seal, Pig, Goat) and make it unclear which class names they should implement and how automated tests will reference types.
issues.suggestedFix: Make class names consistent across problem, template, and solution. Either (A) rename the solution classes to Seal, Pig, and Goat (or implement Seal/Pig/Goat delegating to Space* if retaining Space* variants), and populate Seal.java, Pig.java, Goat.java with the intended implementations; or (B) update the problem statement and template examples to reference SpaceSeal/SpacePig/SpaceGoat explicitly. Ensure the Main/template commented examples and any tests use the same class names.

issues.description: The exercise and template refer to animal classes named Seal, Pig, and Goat (the UML and Main.java use these exact names), but the solution implementation provides classes named SpaceSeal, SpacePig, and SpaceGoat instead (and the expected Seal.java, Pig.java, Goat.java files in the solution are empty). This mismatch means students cannot directly map the problem description and template references to the solution classes and may be confused about which class names they should implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Use consistent class names across artifacts. Either rename SpaceSeal, SpacePig, and SpaceGoat in the solution to Seal, Pig, and Goat respectively (and update their constructors/usages), or provide concrete Seal, Pig, and Goat classes that delegate to or extend the Space* implementations so that the class names in the solution match the UML and template Main.java.
